findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. `proof_list` preserves the worker's heading verbatim. The changed command test supplies `Proof list (run on this commit with -n 2: 3 passed):` and expects it to remain. Close therefore publishes a worker-written result claim regardless of its own run, although Close is meant to write the results and the worker is meant to supply only the item-to-test mapping.
findings.title: Not done: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test دves

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. New evidence beyond the dismissed nested-path finding: the hook writes each node ID relative to that pytest process's working directory. In a monorepo command that runs pytest from `apps/a` and then `apps/b`, both packages' `tests/test_login.py::test_auth` produce the same recorded ID. `proof_list` deduplicates that ID and suffix-matches it to either package's proof entry. A passing test in one package can thus credit an unrun test in the other, or conceal that the other's test was skipped. The two-run test uses one working directory and misses this case.
findings.title: Close merges results from identically named tests in sibling packages

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. For a normal item listing two proofs, such as `tests/test_greeting.py::test_returning, src/greet.test.ts`, the presence of the Python name sends the whole line through `TEST_NAME.sub`. Only the Python name gains a result; the JavaScript name remains bare, with no `not checked` marker. The new test covers JavaScript names only on separate lines, so it passes while this named unmatched test is published without a status.
findings.title: Not done: A mixed-language proof line leaves an unmatched test unmarked

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. A collected test method can be inherited from a shared test class. Pytest then reports, for example, `tests/test_mobile.py::TestMobile::test_login`, while `test_login` is absent from `tests/test_mobile.py` itself. This source-text check returns `not run` before using the exact matching result already found on the preceding line. The command tests define every method in its test file and do not cover inherited tests.
findings.title: Close labels inherited pytest methods not run despite matching run results
